title: Canonical open–closed localization in the constructible Weil heart
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. On a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $S_0$ use the constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] on $S=S_0\times_{k_0}k$, with the common-stage constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Restrictions are the inverse images of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], open extension by zero is the compact-support direct image of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and closed direct image is the direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], all with their induced Weil structures. 
Every open or closed subscheme of $S_0$ is separated and finite type over $k_0$; it and its geometric base change are Noetherian, and the geometric base change is separated and finite type over $k$. The category of constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves is abelian [def-sp-abelian]: its forgetful functor to the constructible heart creates kernels, cokernels and images, and detects short exact sequences. In particular inverse images of subobjects under Weil morphisms are constructible Weil subobjects. Restriction along a locally closed immersion is exact. For an open immersion $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow S_0$ and its complementary closed immersion $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow S_0$, the functors $j_!$ and $i_*$ restrict to exact additive functors of constructible Weil hearts [def-galois-exact-functor; def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. For every constructible Weil sheaf $H$ the actual open counit $\epsilon_H$ and closed unit $\eta_H$ give the Weil-equivariant short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow j_!j^*H\xrightarrow{\epsilon_H}H\xrightarrow{\eta_H}i_*i^*H\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $j,i$ are the geometric base changes of $j_0,i_0$. The assertion includes empty $U_0$ or $Z_0$. On the empty scheme every constructible Weil sheaf is zero.

proof.text: The spectrum of a field is Noetherian: its only ideals are zero and the whole field, and its spectrum has one point. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $S_0$ Noetherian. Every open subscheme $U_0$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Its inclusion is quasi-compact: the inverse image of an affine open is an open subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $S_0$, hence quasi-compact by the same lemma. It is therefore finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. Every closed immersion $Z_0\to S_0$ is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Composition with $S_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Both subschemes are separated over $k_0$ by [lem-trf-immersion-over-separated-base]. Applying the Noetherian lemma again proves the closed-subscheme assertion.

source.place: Final paragraph: canonical open–closed exact sequence, exact extension functors and Weil-equivariant inverse images.

proof.text: For each of $S_0,U_0,Z_0$, [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] makes its geometric base change separated and finite type over $k$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian by the field argument in Step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes each base change Noetherian. This verifies the scheme hypotheses of all the coefficient operations below. The same reasoning applies to the open and closed factors of a locally closed immersion.

source.place: Final paragraph: canonical open–closed exact sequence, exact extension functors and Weil-equivariant inverse images.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C=D^b_c(S,\Qlb)$ and $\mathcal A=\Sh_c(S,\Qlb)$. Its bounded standard $t$-structure is given by [prop-constructible-truncations] and its heart is abelian by [prop-weil-heart-abelian]. Geometric Frobenius $g_S$ is a scheme automorphism. Its prescribed pullback $P=Lg_S^*$ is an exact autoequivalence, with inverse the inverse-automorphism pullback, by [lem-pod-isomorphism-field-transport]. Both pullbacks commute with the standard truncations by [prop-constructible-truncations], so both preserve the two halves. Apply [lem-zl-texact-fixed-pair-heart-cohomology] with $\mathcal D=\mathcal C$, $Q=P$, $F=\operatorname{id}$ and the identity comparison. By [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex](3) its heart fixed pairs are exactly the constructible Weil sheaves in the statement. They are abelian, and forgetting creates kernels and cokernels, with their actual induced invertible Frobenius maps.

source.place: Final paragraph: canonical open–closed exact sequence, exact extension functors and Weil-equivariant inverse images.

proof.text: Images are kernels of cokernels, so the creation of kernels and cokernels in Step 3 also creates images. For an equivariant $u:H\to K$ and Weil subobject $N\hookrightarrow K$, form $K\to\operatorname{coker}(N\hookrightarrow K)$ and take the kernel of its composite with $u$. Its underlying kernel is precisely $u^{-1}N$, hence it is a constructible Weil subobject. A sequence is short exact exactly when its first map is a kernel of its second and its second is a cokernel of its first. The created kernel/cokernel comparisons prove both directions of detection: an underlying isomorphism between fixed pairs is equivariant also in its inverse, obtained by multiplying its intertwining equation by that inverse. Thus underlying short exactness gives short exactness in the Weil heart, and conversely.

source.place: Final paragraph: canonical open–closed exact sequence, exact extension functors and Weil-equivariant inverse images.

proof.text: For a locally closed immersion over $k_0$, [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior](1) applies to the separated finite-type schemes just verified: its prescribed common-stage pullback with induced Weil structure is $t$-exact and restricts to an exact functor of constructible Weil sheaves. Clause (2) of the same node gives $t$-exactness of the actual open compact-support operation and exactness of $j_!$ on constructible Weil sheaves. These are additive functors: the underlying derived coefficient operations are additive and the Weil lift acts on a morphism by that same underlying operation, so it preserves sums and zero morphisms.

source.place: Final paragraph: canonical open–closed exact sequence, exact extension functors and Weil-equivariant inverse images.

proof.text: The closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow S$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Thus [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image] at $\Lambda=\Qlb$ makes the actual $Ri_*$ a $t$-exact functor of the standard constructible categories and its heart restriction exact. The standard Weil lift exists by [prop-weil-operations], with forgetful functor commuting with it. For a short exact sequence of Weil sheaves on $Z_0$, forgetting and applying the underlying exact $i_*^c$ gives a short exact sequence in $\Sh_c(S,\Qlb)$. The lifted arrows are equivariant, and Step 4 detects their short exactness in the Weil heart. This proves exactness of the specified $i_*$, without replacing it by a different functor. Additivity follows because its underlying additive direct image acts on the same Hom groups.

source.place: Final paragraph: canonical open–closed exact sequence, exact extension functors and Weil-equivariant inverse images.

proof.text: Apply [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] to $H$ at $\Lambda=\Qlb$. Its first arrow is exactly the open counit $\epsilon_H$ and its second exactly the closed unit $\eta_H$. Since $j,i$ descend to $k_0$, that node asserts their Weil equivariance. By Steps 5–6, $j_!j^*H$, $H$, and $i_*i^*H$ all lie in the underlying constructible heart. Clause (4) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] therefore turns this underlying distinguished triangle into the short exact sequence with these same two maps. Step 4 detects short exactness in the abelian Weil heart, giving the claimed canonical sequence. No triangulated structure on the category of Weil pairs is used.

source.place: Final paragraph: canonical open–closed exact sequence, exact extension functors and Weil-equivariant inverse images.

proof.text: On the empty scheme every object of its pro-etale site is empty and has the empty covering family. The sheaf condition forces the group of sections of every module sheaf there to be the zero group, so its category of module sheaves has only a zero object [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Complexes, derived-complete subcategories, their rationalizations and the common-stage heart are consequently zero; the sole Weil map on zero is the unique isomorphism. None of the preceding steps required a nonempty scheme. When $U_0=\varnothing$ the left term is zero, and when $Z_0=\varnothing$ the right term is zero, so the same canonical short exact sequence covers both cases (including both empty).

source.place: Final paragraph: canonical open–closed exact sequence, exact extension functors and Weil-equivariant inverse images.
